title: Add rate-limited public JSON feed endpoint for model changelog entries (ETags + caching)
author: Brian Murphy
description: Summary: Adds a customer-facing, machine-readable JSON feed endpoint for published model changelog entries, with IP-based rate limiting, conditional requests via ETag/If-None-Match, and response caching headers. This is the initial MVP target referenced by Support (SUP-18473) and needed for docs-site RSS generation and customer automation. Endpoint: GET /v1/public/changelog/feed.json (new) Returns only status=published entries from the changelog store. Supports pagination and simple filters. Query params: limit (default 50, max 200), cursor (opaque), model_id (optional), since (optional RFC3339), type (optional: addition|update|deprecation|correction). Caching/ETags: - Response includes ETag computed from (latest_published_event_id, latest_published_at, normalized query) so customers can poll cheaply. - Honors If-None-Match; returns 304 with empty body when unchanged. - Cache-Control: public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300. - Adds Vary: Accept-Encoding, X-Redwood-Tenant (defensive; though endpoint is public, we keep future-proofing for tier-gating). Rate limiting: - Adds a dedicated limiter bucket for /v1/public/changelog/feed.json: 60 req/min per IP with burst 10. - Emits 429 with Retry-After. - Uses existing gateway limiter in control plane; no new infra dependency. Observability: - Adds metrics: public_changelog_feed_requests_total{status_code}, public_changelog_feed_304_total, public_changelog_feed_etag_miss_total, public_changelog_feed_rate_limited_total, and p95 latency. - Tracing: span 'public_changelog_feed' includes limit, model_id presence, and cache_hit boolean (etag hit). Security/Privacy notes: - Endpoint reads from the same published representation used by Console. Internal-only fields are not exposed (relies on public allowlist enforced in changelog publish step). - Explicitly rejects requests that attempt to include draft/in_review entries. - Adds minimal abuse mitigations (rate limit + cache headers) but does not implement auth for MVP by design. Testing: - Unit tests for ETag stability and 304 behavior - Integration test for cursor pagination ordering by published_at desc then event_id desc - Gateway test for 429 + Retry-After header Rollout plan: - Ship behind server-side flag PUBLIC_CHANGELOG_FEED_ENABLED (default off in prod) - Enable in staging immediately; prod enable after docs site consumes it (tracked in ENG-4926) Checklist: [x] API reviewed (Console/control plane) [x] Security review requested for rate-limit defaults + caching headers [x] Metrics and dashboards hooks [x] Backward compatibility (new endpoint only) Notes: This does not generate RSS/Atom; docs will convert JSON->RSS in redwood-docs. Also does not implement per-account feeds or webhook push; polling w/ ETag is the intended v1 behavior.

review_conversation: Chloe Martin (review): Can we confirm ordering is deterministic when multiple entries share the same published_at? We saw a similar issue in staging with same-day updates collapsing. Also, please document cursor semantics (opaque vs stable) in the OpenAPI file.

Brian Murphy (author): Yep. Ordering is published_at DESC then event_id DESC (lex compare on ULID) to guarantee deterministic paging. Cursor encodes (published_at,event_id) of the last item. Added explicit note to openapi/public-changelog-feed.yaml and a test covering same timestamp entries.
Logan Wright (review): Metrics look good, but can you add a counter for ETag hits vs misses? It’ll help validate that customers are actually using conditional requests and keep load down.

Brian Murphy (author): Added public_changelog_feed_304_total and public_changelog_feed_etag_miss_total, plus span attribute cache_hit. Also wired to existing http middleware so we capture status codes uniformly.

Marcus Lin (security review): Two asks: (1) ensure no draft entries can slip through even if store query is called incorrectly; (2) rate limit should be separate from other public endpoints so we can tighten without breaking other traffic. Also consider a higher max-age if content changes daily, but I’m ok with 60s for now.

Brian Murphy (author): (1) Handler enforces status==published at the query layer and re-checks before serialization; added a guard that fails closed if status != published. (2) Added a dedicated limiter key 'public_changelog_feed' in limits.yaml. Keeping max-age=60 per PM request for near-real-time publishing; can revisit once we measure.
Ethan Park (review): Please add Retry-After on 429; some enterprise customers will implement polite polling.
Brian Murphy (author): Done. Retry-After set to 60 seconds based on limiter window.
ci_notes: Initial integration-tests run failed due to flaky timing in ratelimit_public_feed_test (asserting exact wait). Updated to assert presence of Retry-After and 429 count, and reran; green.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Chloe Martin
release_notes: New public endpoint: GET /v1/public/changelog/feed.json for published model changelog entries
Supports pagination + basic filters and conditional GET via ETag/If-None-Match (304)
Adds IP rate limiting and cache headers to reduce load during polling
